name: Wrong Order Delivery
blurb: Two neighbours swap mixed-up takeaway and start a silent war over who ordered better
title: Wrong Order Delivery: 45-Second Comedy Skit Script for 2
description: A 45-second vertical comedy script for 2: neighbours swap mixed-up takeaway, then battle over whose dinner is better. Free to film and perform.
h1: Wrong Order Delivery: a 45-Second Comedy Script for 2 People
logline: Two neighbours open their doors at the same moment, each holding the other's takeaway. The swap is perfectly polite, until each of them realises the other one ordered better.
setting: A hallway with two facing front doors, at night. Props: two takeaway bags (noodles and dumplings), chopsticks, two phones.

roles.name: Mia
roles.note: Written as a woman, any gender works, 18+. Lives on the left. Proud of her noodles, secretly wants the dumplings.

roles.name: Leo
roles.note: Written as a man, any gender works, 18+. Lives on the right. Calm on the outside, very competitive about food.

script.scene: INT. HALLWAY BETWEEN TWO FLATS – NIGHT

script.action: Two doors open at the same moment. MIA and LEO each hold a takeaway bag.
They swap. Polite nods. Both doors close.
Both doors open a crack. Both sniff the air.

script.say: His had extra sauce. I saw it.

script.action: Mia eats noodles in her doorway, slowly, loudly. Leo answers with a dumpling, eyes locked on hers.
Without breaking eye contact, both tap at their phones.

script.sfx: Two order chimes, one after the other.

script.action: Both doors open. Each holds a new bag. They read the labels and freeze.

script.say: You ordered my noodles. And they came to me.
You ordered my dumplings. And they came to me.

script.action: A long beat. Mia sits down on the hallway floor. Leo sits opposite. They hold out their boxes.

head: Shot
What we see / hear
Seconds
rows: Both doors open at once, each holding the wrong bag
The polite swap, nods, doors close
Doors open a crack, sniffing, both lines to camera
Loud eating, the tiny dumplings exchange
Doorbells, new bags, reading labels, the twist lines
Both sit on the floor and share, last lines

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 with the phone at chest height in the middle of the hallway, so you can pan between the two doors without moving. A warm hallway light is enough; switch off a harsh ceiling light if it flattens faces. Record sound close to the actors or add a clip-on microphone, because the eating noises are part of the joke. One person can play both roles: lock the phone on a small tripod, film all of Mia's side, then all of Leo's, and cut them together. Plan on three or four takes per shot.

ul: Play the first swap completely sincere. The rivalry only works if they start out genuinely nice.
The lines to camera are confessions. Say them quietly, as if the neighbour might hear through the door.
The loud eating is a silent duel: hold eye contact and chew slower than feels natural.
Pause a full second after reading the new labels. Let the audience work out the twist before Mia says it.
Common mistake: shouting. Keep every line at polite-neighbour volume; the pettiness is funnier quiet.
Move it to an office: two coworkers get each other's lunch from the shared fridge, and the rivalry plays out across the desks.
Make it three doors on one landing, so the third neighbour keeps receiving everyone's orders and eating them.
Part-two hook: the next night a single bag arrives with both names on it, and neither of them ordered it.

faq.q: Can I post this on a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0, including for monetised videos and ads. Put "Script: cv.cm" in the caption or description.

Yes. Put the phone on a tripod in the middle of the hallway, film every Mia shot, change your top, then film every Leo shot and cut them together. The doors never need to be in the same shot with both actors.
Anything two people would order on a delivery app and could be jealous of. Pick two dishes that look different on camera, and change the words noodles and dumplings to match.
